The two interleave in practice. Magnet energization is a commissioning milestone that also produces the evidence for the magnet gate G2. First plasma is a commissioning milestone that opens the ramp toward the confinement gate G1. First tritium is where fuel-loop commissioning and the fuel-loop gate G3 coincide. So each physics gate rides on a commissioning milestone, but the gate is judged on measured performance against prediction, while the commissioning milestone is judged only on the subsystem working.

Both apply to a machine not yet built. Keeping them distinct is part of how the program avoids the overclaiming that has damaged fusion, first plasma is a real milestone, but it is not gain, and it is not first tritium.

title: NOAK Improvements
lede: Nth-of-a-kind units apply the build and operability lessons of the first machine while holding the physics design point fixed.
body: The nth-of-a-kind (NOAK) units are where the program applies what the first machine taught. The physics design point, Q_sci 3.076, 85.0 MW, 16.84 T, 9.66 MA, stays essentially fixed once validated. What changes is how the machine is built and operated: faster, more reliably, and with less unnecessary instrumentation.
Shorter build than the roughly 3.5-year FOAK, from procurement and assembly lessons
Streamlined diagnostics, keeping what proved essential at FOAK
Improved remote-maintenance access to raise foundry availability
Manufacturing steps standardized where FOAK was bespoke

Once FOAK validates the design point at the gates, changing the physics would reopen retired risk. NOAK deliberately holds the validated physics constant and concentrates improvement on build time and operability, which is where the largest, safest gains are available after the first unit.

FOAK retires physics risk; NOAK retires operability risk, whether the machine can be built repeatably and run at high availability as a foundry. This is the second stage of the learning curve, between proving the machine and standardizing it.
NOAK improvements describe planned second-stage units for a machine not yet built. They are informed by FOAK measurement and quality-assurance data, and they are the bridge to BOAK standardization.

title: BOAK Standardization
lede: Best-of-a-kind units settle the design as a repeatable, manufactured product with known lead times and predictable foundry output.
body: Best-of-a-kind (BOAK) is the endpoint of the learning curve: the design settled into a repeatable, manufactured product. By this stage the physics is validated, the build is proven, and the machine can be produced with known lead times and predictable output, exactly what a foundry needs.
A fixed, documented design suitable for repeatable fabrication
Known lead times for long-lead items like magnets and vessel
Predictable output: the tritium class and helium-3 coproduct per unit
High, reproducible availability from mature maintenance design

A small foundry fleet needs its units to be alike so that supply is predictable and operation is uniform. Standardization at BOAK turns a set of individually built machines into a product line, which is what makes a reliable isotope and neutron supply possible.
The end of the risk program

By BOAK, the major physics, engineering, and operability risks have been retired, at G1, G2, and G3 on FOAK, and through NOAK build and operation. BOAK is not about discovery; it is about consistency. This is the stage where the breeder is genuinely a foundry rather than an experiment.

BOAK describes the intended settled form of a machine not yet built. It is the goal the FOAK-to-NOAK-to-BOAK sequence is organized to reach, and the basis for keeping the breeder fleet small and supply-driven.

title: Schedule and Milestones
lede: A compact timeline from Q2 2027 construction start through first plasma, the physics gates, and first tritium near 2030.
body: The first-of-a-kind breeder follows a defined sequence of milestones, each dependent on the one before. The schedule below is a plan for a machine not yet built; it is stated as intent, with schedule risk retired by execution rather than assumed away.
Q2 2027 / Construction begins; long-lead magnet and vessel procurement
2027-2029 / Fabrication and assembly from the centerpost outward
Commissioning / Vacuum, cryogenics, magnet energization (G2), first plasma
Ramp / Build to design point; confinement gate (G1)

Long-lead procurement gates the whole schedule, which is why it begins at construction start. Commissioning cannot begin until assembly is complete; the physics gates cannot be judged until the relevant subsystems are commissioned; first tritium cannot happen until confinement and field are demonstrated. The chain is strict.

Beyond first tritium, the program moves to NOAK and BOAK units, which are planned to build faster than the roughly 3.5-year FOAK as procurement and assembly mature. The breeder fleet remains small, sized to isotope demand.
Every date here is a target for a machine not yet built. No hardware net-gain, and indeed no net electricity, is claimed at any milestone; the breeder's demonstration is gain and first tritium.

title: What FOAK Does Not Prove
lede: The first-of-a-kind unit proves gain and first tritium; it does not prove net electricity, fleet reproducibility, or burner physics.
body: Being explicit about what a demonstration does not show is as important as stating what it does. The first-of-a-kind (FOAK) breeder is designed to prove fusion gain and the foundry function through first tritium. Several things it will not prove, and the program does not claim it will.
Net electricity: the breeder does not target net electric output at all
Fleet reproducibility: repeatable build and high availability are NOAK and BOAK work
Long-term component life: full-life neutron fluence on the centerpost accrues over years
Burner physics: the D-3He burner is a separate machine and program

Overclaiming from a first demonstration is a recurring failure mode in fusion. A machine that reaches gain and breeds tritium is a genuine achievement, and it is enough for the foundry mission. Stretching it into claims about net power or fleet economics would be dishonest and is refused.

FOAK proves that the design point, validated at G1, G2, and G3, produces neutrons, breeds tritium, and yields the product stream. That is the claim, bounded and reported against pre-registered predictions, no more and no less.
FOAK is a machine not yet built. This page states, in advance, the limits of what its eventual success will and will not establish.

title: Open Questions and Reconciliations
lede: The program tracks specific unresolved questions honestly, including net breeding ratio and centerpost lifetime, mapped to the gates that settle them.
body: A credible design states what it has not yet resolved. The breeder program tracks specific open questions and reconciliations rather than presenting the design as finished. Each is mapped to the gate, test, or analysis that will settle it.
Breeding ratio: design-level TBR of 1.8 versus net three-dimensional breeding in a real blanket, settled by measurement at G3
Centerpost lifetime: neutron fluence on the conductors over the machine's operating life
Magnet materials: some REBCO material and author-attribution details under reconciliation
Confinement scaling: whether the plasma reaches Q_sci 3.076 at delta -0.30, settled at G1

Open items are not hidden or smoothed over. They are documented, assigned to a gate or analysis, and reported against pre-registered predictions when tested. The tritium breeding reconciliation, in particular, is a headline example: the design uses TBR as a lever precisely because the net value is uncertain until G3.

The value of the breeder program is a rigorous design and a concrete build plan, not a claim of finished physics. Stating open questions plainly is what separates a serious program from marketing. The gates exist to close these questions with data.
These questions concern a machine not yet built. Their resolution is the substance of what the first-of-a-kind unit and its gate program are designed to deliver.
